With no pattern by user or route, I'd look for something cross-cutting: token verification (clock skew, key rotation or cache), a single bad pod, or timing around deploys. I'll pull the 401 responses from the logs with their request ids and compare pod, time, and token age and expiry to find what the failing ones share.
Action: Read the auth middleware, then collect a sample of the 401s from the logs and look for the common factor.

A one-cent mismatch like this usually means the total is rounded differently from the line amounts that are displayed, for example rounding once at the end instead of per line. I haven't looked at the code yet, so I'd confirm that rather than assume. Also, invoices already issued may have stored totals that a fix won't change.
Action: Find the totals calculation, write a failing test with a multi-line case that reproduces the off-by-one, then fix it so the shown lines sum to the total.

Feature flags are managed in GrowthBook. The invoices export command is already planned behind the flag `cli-invoices-export`, which as of my last note still needed to be created in GrowthBook. For beta orgs only, you'd target on an org attribute, so I need to check what attributes the code passes to the flag evaluation.
Action: Check how flags are read in the code, see whether the flag has been created yet, and ask if you want this same flag or a new one for the beta orgs.

I'll add the monthly invoice export bucket in infra as private with a 90 day expiry on objects, and put the `team` and `env` cost tags on it since Priya's script flags anything without them. I'll copy the team value from existing resources rather than guess it. One thing to confirm: an earlier note describes an exports bucket with a 30 day expiry, so is this a new bucket or the same one with a different retention?
Action: Look at the infra code for how buckets are defined, then draft the bucket and check it with a plan without applying it.

Duplicate header rows usually mean the CSV helper already writes the header and the button adds its own on top. I'll look at the expenses export button and the helper it calls and remove the extra header. I'll also add a regression test that asserts exactly one header line.
Action: Read the export button and CSV helper, fix it, add the test, and run the expenses tests.

I'll check the existing schema for conventions and for a UUID v7 generator already in use, so the new primary key is v7, not serial or v4. The table has the invoice id as a foreign key, sent_at, channel as an enum of email and sms, and status. You haven't said what the allowed status values are, so I'd ask rather than invent them.
Action: Look at the existing drizzle schema, then add the payment_reminders table, generate the migration, and ask for the status values.

I'll add `memo: z.string().max(500).optional()` to the request schema in apps/api/src/schemas and wire it through to storage, checking whether a column and migration are needed. The OpenAPI spec is generated from the zod schemas, so I'll regenerate it with `pnpm turbo run openapi --filter api` and never hand-edit the YAML. Since this is public behavior, I'll also update the relevant docs/ page.
Action: Update the schema, regenerate the spec, update the docs, and add tests for the length limit.

I'll add tsx as a devDependency of packages/cli with pnpm so the lockfile updates with it, and point the scripts in packages/cli/scripts at the TypeScript sources directly. I'll check what the existing package.json scripts call so they no longer need a build first.
Action: Run the install in packages/cli, update the scripts, run one of them to confirm it works, and tell you which files changed including the lockfile.

I'll replace the switch with a typed map from event type to handler, keeping behavior identical: unknown event types fall through the same way the switch default does, and the idempotent stripe_events storage path stays untouched. This is billing code and your raw-body change is still uncommitted, so I'd keep this refactor separate and leave both for your review before any commit.
Action: Do the refactor, run the api tests and the replayed Stripe events, and show you the diff.

That sounds like a slog, new laptop setups always are. The deps are installed in the new clone, and the full test suite I kicked off there is still running, so I don't have a result to share yet.
Action: Check on the test run and report the result, and remind you that Postgres and DATABASE_URL are still needed for the seed.

I'll write a Playwright spec that goes through the full flow (new invoice, pick client, add a line, save, send) against the local dev server. The web dev server needs to be up on port 3000 first, with the database and Redis containers running, and then `pnpm --filter web e2e` runs it. There is a known unrelated failure in invoices/detail.spec.ts ('downloads pdf' 404s because the seed invoice has no pdfKey), so I won't mistake that for mine.
Action: Bring up the dev environment, write the spec in the e2e folder, and run it.

Parking the bucket. Looking at invoice-number.ts now.
Action: Read the file and the test setup, reproduce the collision with parallel runs, then fix it.

That error means `InvoiceLineItems` called `.map` on a value that was undefined at line 24, so some invoice reached it without its line items. The trace doesn't say why, and I wouldn't guess whether it's the api omitting the field or the component getting the wrong data. It would help to know which invoice Lena hit.
Action: Open InvoiceLineItems.tsx and InvoiceDetail.tsx, trace where the prop comes from, and ask Lena for the invoice id.

My notes say a /pricing page already exists under app/(marketing)/pricing with placeholder prices that marketing still has to confirm, so I'd verify what's there before building a new one. It must be listed as public in the Clerk middleware, and colors should use theme tokens. /settings/team is for signed-in users, so it goes under app/(dashboard)/settings/team/page.tsx.
Action: Check the existing pricing page and middleware, then build the team members page.

I'll build the company profile form the way the other forms in apps/web do it, with react-hook-form and a zod schema through zodResolver, looking at settings/org-form.tsx as the example. Name and the sender email are required (email validated), and tax id is optional. I need to check which api endpoint saves it rather than assume.
Action: Read org-form.tsx, create the company profile form and schema, wire it to the existing settings endpoint, and add tests.

I'll grep case-insensitively for 'recieved' in apps/api and services/worker and fix the spelling in comments, logs and strings. If any hit is a public response value or an identifier that clients might depend on, I'll leave it and flag it, since changing it could be an API change.
Action: Run the grep, fix the safe ones, run the worker and api tests, and list anything I left alone.

Good, the tag stays as team=payments. For the double submit, add `hx-disabled-elt="this"` on the form's submit button or form, and `hx-sync="this:drop"` on the form so a second request is dropped while the first is in flight. Depending on your htmx version, hx-disabled-elt may need a recent one. For real protection against duplicates, also guard server-side (for example, a unique constraint or idempotency check).
Action: Check your htmx version and the form markup if you want me to apply it.

Leaving the api one as is. The worker spelling fixes stay, and the worker tests passed. The api test run is still going.
Action: Wait for the api tests and report the result.

An 'ok' doesn't tell me which framework the API is on, so I'll read it from apps/api/package.json instead of waiting. The tests and the typecheck both came back green, with no failures.
Action: Find the framework and major version, then write the x-org-id guard in that framework's style and register it on the org-scoped routes only.

Glad it helps. If this becomes a ticket, I'll keep it out of #1192 and do it on a separate branch and PR, as asked. It would be a server-side export covering all invoices including voided ones, with the fixed columns they listed.
Action: Wait for your go-ahead before starting.

You're welcome. The full web unit suite and the typecheck are still running, so I have nothing to report on them yet.
Action: Check the results and post them when they finish.

I'll add a `--since <date>` option to `acme invoices export` that validates the YYYY-MM-DD format and passes it to the api as the `since` query param on each paginated request. Invalid dates will give a clear error before any request goes out. I'll update the command's help text too.
Action: Find the export command in the CLI, add the option and validation, and add tests.

I'll scaffold `acme invoices list` next to the clients command, following its structure: it calls GET /v1/invoices and prints a table. Per your rule, it supports `--json`, printing plain JSON to stdout with no table or colors, so people can pipe it into jq.
Action: Read the clients command, create the invoices list command with table and --json output, and add tests for both.

Next passes a `digest` on the error object given to global-error.tsx, so the fix is to attach `error.digest` as a tag when we call Sentry's captureException. That lets you search Sentry by digest and match the server logs. The request id idea (x-request-id from the web client) was proposed but not approved, so I'll leave it out of this change.
Action: Read global-error.tsx, add the digest as a Sentry tag, and add a test.

I'll check which lockfile the fresh clone has to pick the right package manager, install from it, and confirm the seed package builds. One thing to watch: scripts/seed-demo is new and the ESM fixes were made in your other checkout, so the clone won't have them unless they're committed and pushed. The seed also needs a running Postgres and its connection string.
Action: Run the install in ~/code/acme-platform, then verify seed-demo is present and builds there.
